findings.issue_text: In produce_to_pipe mode, _ensure_processes_alive tries to kill a threading.Thread (which cannot be killed) on hang detection, spawning duplicate flusher threads polling the same shards that compete for segments and can duplicate spans to Kafka

Memory backpressure calculation double-counts cluster nodes when a node's shards are split across multiple shard-group buffers, distorting used/available ratio and tripping max_memory_percentage too early or too late
Metric tag key typo: produce timer uses tags={"shard": ...} but wait timer uses tags={"shards": ...}, splitting dashboards/alerts keyed on shard
flusher_processes=0 is falsy so __init__ treats it as one process per shard (maximum fan-out) instead of rejecting the invalid/off config
join() timeout path breaks out mid-loop, skipping terminate() for all not-yet-iterated processes, leaving child processes running and polling Redis/producing to Kafka after strategy closure
Per-shard-group buffers multiply Redis health-check load per submit(): record_stored_segments() and get_memory_info() now called once per buffer per message, multiplying hot-path cost

Per-shard process explosion: when flusher_processes is not set, default is one spawned process per assigned shard, each with its own Kafka producer, Redis connections, and Sentry SDK state, causing unbounded memory/FD explosion with many partitions

Killed processes are never joined: _ensure_processes_alive calls process.kill() then overwrites self.processes[process_index] without join(), causing zombie accumulation and leaked resources across restarts

available memory is double-counted across per-shard buffers: summing memory_infos.available from overlapping per-process buffers inflates the denominator, making memory pressure read artificially low and weakening the backpressure check

join(timeout) breaks out of the outer loop entirely on timeout, leaving later processes un-terminated so orphaned flusher processes can outlive the consumer and keep producing to Kafka / polling Redis after shutdown

Per-shard-group SpansBuffer constructed on every restart: new buffers constructed in the parent per process group diverge from the factory-owned buffer that can only be pickled by the Process, risking different buffer instances and re-paying construction cost on restart churn
Dead code: _create_process_for_shard is never called; it also has a hazard of creating a second live process for shards already owned by a running process without killing it

Hung threads cannot be killed: kill path guarded by isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process), so a hung thread in test/thread mode is never stopped while a replacement thread is created for the same shards, duplicating production of spans

Unhealthy metric fan-out: metrics.incr('spans.buffer.flusher_unhealthy') is emitted per shard per submit() call while a process is unhealthy rather than once per incident, multiplying metric cardinality and volume

Thread-mode restart never stops the old worker: process.kill() raises AttributeError on a Thread and is swallowed, so a new thread is created while the old one keeps running, causing duplicate flushers racing on the same shards, duplicate Kafka production, and double accounting
No validation of flusher_processes: a negative value results in zero flusher processes created, causing silent data stagnation as spans accumulate in Redis without flushing or health-check failure
join() breaks out when remaining_time <= 0, skipping terminate() for remaining processes, so a stuck process can keep producing to Kafka during/after consumer shutdown
Killed/crashed processes are never join()ed before replacement, accumulating zombies and their shared-memory segments across restart cycles
Dead code _create_process_for_shard (singular) never kills/reaps the old process and would corrupt state if ever called; it should be removed or routed through the restart path
process_restarts is never reset after sustained health, so one shard's process hitting MAX_PROCESS_RESTARTS cumulatively can crash the whole consumer long after a transient incident
Inconsistent metric tag names: produce timer uses tags={"shards": ...} while other metrics use "shard", splitting/losing telemetry on produce latency

New multi-process health/restart logic (restart counter, RuntimeError after MAX_PROCESS_RESTARTS, per-process hang detection in flusher.py _ensure_processes_alive) has zero test coverage despite being the most behaviorally risky change

Tests only exercise the threading path because they pass produce_to_pipe=messages.append, so the multiprocessing spawn path (pickling shard_buffer, mp_context.Value handles, process.kill()/terminate()) is never verified

test_flusher_processes_limit verifies structure not behavior — it asserts process count and shard counts but never submits a message or verifies spans from multiplexed shards actually get flushed, and round-robin shard distribution is unasserted

Weakened assertion in test_flusher backpressure test: changed from checking aggregate backpressure_since.value to any(x.value for per-process values), so aggregate backpressure behavior in submit() raising MessageRejected is not verified and there is no test for MessageRejected on single-process sustained backpressure
Missing edge-case test: empty assigned_shards causes ZeroDivisionError at construction because num_processes = min(max_processes, len(assigned_shards)) can be 0 and i % num_processes divides by zero

Flaky timing in test_basic: fixed time.sleep(0.1) with no synchronization guaranteeing the flusher thread completed, making (msg,) = messages assertion racy on slow CI — should use explicit wait/poll loop
No test for flusher_processes CLI wiring: the --flusher-processes click option → factory parameter → SpanFlusher(max_processes=...) chain is untested, so name/param drift would go unnoticed
Dead code: `_create_process_for_shard` in flusher.py is never called and duplicates process-lookup logic, risking divergence
Inconsistent metric tag key: `wait_produce` uses `tags={"shards": shard_tag}` while other metrics use `"shard"`, fragmenting metrics and breaking dashboards/alerts
Test's added `time.sleep(0.1)` is a no-op because `time.sleep` is globally monkeypatched, providing no synchronization and risking flaky tests
Unrelated drive-by change to CLAUDE.md (hasattr vs isinstance guidance) bundled into this PR, muddying review and git blame

No validation of `flusher_processes` / `max_processes`: negative `max_processes` yields zero flusher processes with no error, `0` is silently coerced via `or` fallback inconsistently with CLI semantics
Restart path leaks hung threads / duplicate flushers for same shards: threads cannot be killed, and the `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)` guard makes the kill a silent no-op for threads
Misleading dead comment `# Check if any shard handled by this process is unhealthy` precedes a plain `cause = "hang"` with no per-shard check and should be deleted
Duplicated metric-emission loops across `submit` paths couple submit's backpressure logic to internal shard→process partitioning; should be extracted into aggregate helpers
join() timeout path breaks out of the loop, skipping terminate() for current and remaining flusher processes, causing partial-failure shutdown regression (process 1 terminated, processes 2..N not)
Group restart cascade in _ensure_processes_alive: a hung shard kills and restarts its whole process group, dragging healthy sibling shards down on every restart cycle
Per-group restart counter means a flapping group trips MAX_PROCESS_RESTARTS and raises RuntimeError, restarting the consumer and punishing shards that were fine

Shared healthy_since is only updated after a full loop over all shards, so a shard that repeatedly hangs-and-recovers under a fast sibling never accumulates unhealthy time — shard-level hang detection effectively never fires

Hung thread-mode flushers are never actually killed: the kill is guarded by isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process) so it's a no-op for threading.Thread, while a new thread is still spawned for the same shards, allowing N hung threads to accumulate and poll the same shard groups concurrently, with double-produce risk if a hung thread wakes after the replacement flushed segments
Metrics tag typo: wait_produce metric uses tags={"shards": shard_tag} while every other metric uses "shard", splitting the metric into a separate tag family and breaking dashboards/alerts

Dead/incorrect method _create_process_for_shard is never called and its semantics (restart entire group for one shard) invite misuse by future callers; should be deleted or made to delegate to the group path

Metrics cardinality explosion: segment_size_bytes and flusher_unhealthy now tag raw shard numbers, and flusher_unhealthy fires per shard per unhealthy event, multiplying series cardinality with many partitions

adjudication_records.issue_text: In produce_to_pipe mode, _ensure_processes_alive tries to kill a threading.Thread (which cannot be killed) on hang detection, spawning duplicate flusher threads polling the same shards that compete for segments and can duplicate spans to Kafka

adjudication.rationale: In `SpanFlusher._create_process_for_shards`, when `produce_to_pipe` is set it uses `threading.Thread` (not a multiprocessing process): `make_process = threading.Thread`. In `_ensure_processes_alive`, on hang detection (`time.time() - process_healthy_since[...] > max_unhealthy_seconds`) it attempts to stop the worker only via `if isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process): process.kill()`, which is a no-op for threads. It then unconditionally calls `_create_process_for_shards(...)`, starting a new thread for the same shard set while the old thread is still alive, leading to multiple flusher threads polling the same shards concurrently (and potentially producing duplicate/conflicting work).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Memory backpressure calculation double-counts cluster nodes when a node's shards are split across multiple shard-group buffers, distorting used/available ratio and tripping max_memory_percentage too early or too late

adjudication.rationale: In `SpanFlusher.submit`, the memory backpressure check changed from a single `self.buffer.get_memory_info()` call to aggregating across all per-process shard buffers: `memory_infos = []; for buffer in self.buffers.values(): memory_infos.extend(buffer.get_memory_info()); used = sum(...); available = sum(...)`. If `get_memory_info()` reports memory at a shared service/node level (e.g., Redis cluster nodes) rather than strictly disjoint per-shard resources, this new aggregation can double-count the same node’s used/available when that node serves shards that are now split across multiple `SpansBuffer` instances, skewing the used/available ratio and thus the `max_memory_percentage` decision. The diff doesn’t show `get_memory_info()`’s semantics, so it’s a concrete risk/edge-case introduced by the change but not provably a definite defect from this diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Metric tag key typo: produce timer uses tags={"shard": ...} but wait timer uses tags={"shards": ...}, splitting dashboards/alerts keyed on shard
flusher_processes=0 is falsy so __init__ treats it as one process per shard (maximum fan-out) instead of rejecting the invalid/off config

adjudication.rationale: In `SpanFlusher.__init__`, the line `self.max_processes = max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)` treats `0` as falsy. Since the new CLI option `--flusher-processes` is `type=int` with no validation and the factory forwards `flusher_processes` to `SpanFlusher(max_processes=...)`, a user setting `--flusher-processes=0` would be interpreted as `len(buffer.assigned_shards)` (max fan-out) rather than being rejected or resulting in 0. This is a real behavioral defect introduced by the new option/parameter plumbing.

adjudication_records.issue_text: join() timeout path breaks out mid-loop, skipping terminate() for all not-yet-iterated processes, leaving child processes running and polling Redis/producing to Kafka after strategy closure
matched_golden_ids: Breaking out of the loop when the deadline has elapsed can skip terminating remaining flusher processes, potentially leaving them running after shutdown; consider ensuring termination is attempted even if the deadline is exceeded.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both comments identify that on a timeout/deadline path the code breaks out of the loop early, which prevents terminate/cleanup from being applied to remaining flusher processes, potentially leaving them running after shutdown.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Per-shard-group buffers multiply Redis health-check load per submit(): record_stored_segments() and get_memory_info() now called once per buffer per message, multiplying hot-path cost

adjudication.rationale: In `SpanFlusher.submit()`, the diff changes single-buffer calls to per-process/per-shard-group loops: `for buffer in self.buffers.values(): buffer.record_stored_segments()` and similarly `for buffer in self.buffers.values(): memory_infos.extend(buffer.get_memory_info())`. Previously these were called once on `self.buffer`. Since `self.buffers` is populated with one `SpansBuffer(shards)` per flusher process in `_create_process_for_shards`, this multiplies the work per `submit()` by the number of flusher processes/shard groups, which could increase Redis-related polling/health-check overhead. This is a performance/architecture concern rather than a direct correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Per-shard process explosion: when flusher_processes is not set, default is one spawned process per assigned shard, each with its own Kafka producer, Redis connections, and Sentry SDK state, causing unbounded memory/FD explosion with many partitions

adjudication.rationale: In `SpanFlusher.__init__`, the default is now `self.max_processes = max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)` and `self.num_processes = min(self.max_processes, len(buffer.assigned_shards))`, so when `flusher_processes`/`max_processes` is unset it results in `num_processes == len(assigned_shards)` (i.e., one process per shard) via `process_to_shards_map` and `_create_processes()`. This is a concrete behavior change from the prior single-process model and can create large numbers of processes with many partitions/shards. While this is primarily an operational/scaling concern (resource usage) rather than an immediate correctness defect, it is diff-grounded and significant.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Killed processes are never joined: _ensure_processes_alive calls process.kill() then overwrites self.processes[process_index] without join(), causing zombie accumulation and leaked resources across restarts

adjudication.rationale: In `SpanFlusher._ensure_processes_alive`, when a `multiprocessing.Process` is deemed unhealthy it calls `process.kill()` and then immediately recreates/replaces it via `_create_process_for_shards(process_index, shards)` (which overwrites `self.processes[process_index]`). There is no `process.join()` (or equivalent wait) on the killed process before it is discarded, so terminated child processes may not be reaped, leading to zombie processes / leaked OS resources across repeated restarts. The later `join()` method only terminates current entries in `self.processes`, not any prior killed/replaced processes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: available memory is double-counted across per-shard buffers: summing memory_infos.available from overlapping per-process buffers inflates the denominator, making memory pressure read artificially low and weakening the backpressure check

adjudication.rationale: In `SpanFlusher.submit`, the diff changes memory aggregation from `list(self.buffer.get_memory_info())` to extending from each per-process `SpansBuffer` in `self.buffers` (created with disjoint shard subsets via `process_to_shards_map`). The diff shows shards are partitioned across buffers (no overlap), so it does not show `available` being double-counted due to overlapping buffers. Whether `get_memory_info()` returns per-shard vs global/shared memory info is not shown here, and the same potential summing issue could already have existed when a single `SpansBuffer` held multiple shards. Thus the specific claim of denominator inflation from overlapping per-process buffers is not verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: join(timeout) breaks out of the outer loop entirely on timeout, leaving later processes un-terminated so orphaned flusher processes can outlive the consumer and keep producing to Kafka / polling Redis after shutdown

adjudication.rationale: In SpanFlusher.join(), the code iterates `for process_index, process in self.processes.items():` and if `deadline` has passed it executes `break`, which exits the entire loop and skips waiting/terminating any remaining processes. Since termination (`process.terminate()`) is only applied inside the loop per-process, later processes can be left running past shutdown when a timeout occurs.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Per-shard-group SpansBuffer constructed on every restart: new buffers constructed in the parent per process group diverge from the factory-owned buffer that can only be pickled by the Process, risking different buffer instances and re-paying construction cost on restart churn

adjudication.rationale: In `SpanFlusher._create_process_for_shards` the code constructs a fresh `SpansBuffer(shards)` in the parent every time a process is created/restarted, stores it in `self.buffers`, and also passes it to the spawned process (`partial(SpanFlusher.main, shard_buffer)`). With `spawn`, the child will operate on an unpickled copy, while the parent continues to use its own instance for `record_stored_segments()` and `get_memory_info()` (now iterating `self.buffers.values()`), so there are indeed multiple buffer instances per shard-group and they get recreated on restart churn. The diff doesn’t prove this causes incorrect behavior (buffer methods may just hit Redis), but it is a concrete architecture/perf/state-divergence concern introduced by this change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Dead code: _create_process_for_shard is never called; it also has a hazard of creating a second live process for shards already owned by a running process without killing it

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `SpanFlusher._create_process_for_shard` is newly added but never referenced/called anywhere (`_ensure_processes_alive` restarts via `_create_process_for_shards`, and no other call sites appear). The method also calls `_create_process_for_shards(...)` directly without first killing/terminating the existing process for that `process_index`, so if it were invoked it could spawn an additional live process while overwriting `self.processes[process_index]` with the new one, losing the handle to the old process.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Hung threads cannot be killed: kill path guarded by isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process), so a hung thread in test/thread mode is never stopped while a replacement thread is created for the same shards, duplicating production of spans

adjudication.rationale: In thread mode (when `produce_to_pipe` is set), `_create_process_for_shards` creates a `threading.Thread` and stores it in `self.processes`. In `_ensure_processes_alive`, the restart path only attempts to stop the old worker if `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)` (it calls `process.kill()` only then). For a hung/unhealthy thread (`cause == "hang"` based on `process_healthy_since[...]`), the code will start a replacement thread via `_create_process_for_shards(...)` but never stops the old one, and it overwrites `self.processes[process_index]` with the new thread handle. This can leave the old thread running and potentially flushing/producing concurrently for the same shards, causing duplicate production.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Unhealthy metric fan-out: metrics.incr('spans.buffer.flusher_unhealthy') is emitted per shard per submit() call while a process is unhealthy rather than once per incident, multiplying metric cardinality and volume

adjudication.rationale: In `SpanFlusher.submit()` the diff now calls `_ensure_processes_alive()` on every submit. In `_ensure_processes_alive()`, when a process is unhealthy it executes `for shard in shards: metrics.incr("spans.buffer.flusher_unhealthy", tags={"cause": cause, "shard": shard})`, which will emit one metric per shard on every subsequent `submit()` while the process remains unhealthy (no throttling/"emit once" guard). This can multiply metric volume/cardinality, but it’s an operational/observability concern rather than a functional correctness defect shown by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Thread-mode restart never stops the old worker: process.kill() raises AttributeError on a Thread and is swallowed, so a new thread is created while the old one keeps running, causing duplicate flushers racing on the same shards, duplicate Kafka production, and double accounting

adjudication.rationale: In thread-mode (`produce_to_pipe is not None`), `_create_process_for_shards` creates a `threading.Thread` and stores it in `self.processes`. On unhealthy detection, `_ensure_processes_alive` restarts by calling `_create_process_for_shards(...)` but only attempts to stop the old worker if `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)`; for a `threading.Thread` it does nothing (the `kill()` branch is skipped, and the exception handler wouldn’t help). If the thread is still alive but marked unhealthy via the `healthy_since` hang check, a new thread is started for the same shard set while the old one can continue running, leading to concurrent flushers for the same shards (duplicate work/production/accounting). This behavior is directly implied by the diff in `_ensure_processes_alive` and `_create_process_for_shards`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No validation of flusher_processes: a negative value results in zero flusher processes created, causing silent data stagnation as spans accumulate in Redis without flushing or health-check failure

adjudication.rationale: The diff indeed adds `flusher_processes` without explicit validation (click option is just `type=int`), but the described outcome is not supported. In `SpanFlusher.__init__`, `self.max_processes = max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)` means a negative value is truthy and will be used; then `self.num_processes = min(self.max_processes, len(...))` can become negative. That leads to `process_to_shards_map` being empty (`range(self.num_processes)`), and the subsequent shard assignment does `process_index = i % self.num_processes` and `self.process_to_shards_map[process_index].append(...)`, which would raise (e.g., KeyError), i.e., a crash rather than "zero processes" with silent stagnation and no health-check failure.

adjudication_records.issue_text: join() breaks out when remaining_time <= 0, skipping terminate() for remaining processes, so a stuck process can keep producing to Kafka during/after consumer shutdown

adjudication.rationale: In SpanFlusher.join(), the loop over self.processes breaks out entirely when remaining_time <= 0 ("break" inside the for-loop). That means any later processes in self.processes will not reach the per-process termination logic (the `if isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process): process.terminate()` at the end of the loop body). With a finite timeout, this can leave some flusher processes running after consumer shutdown is proceeding, despite `self.stopped.value = True`, which is exactly the kind of stuck/hung process scenario the finding describes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Killed/crashed processes are never join()ed before replacement, accumulating zombies and their shared-memory segments across restart cycles

adjudication.rationale: In `SpanFlusher._ensure_processes_alive`, an unhealthy `multiprocessing.Process` is `kill()`ed and immediately replaced via `_create_process_for_shards(...)` without any `join()`/wait on the old process (and the reference in `self.processes[process_index]` is overwritten). This can leave terminated child processes as zombies until reaped. Similarly, `join()` waits in a loop for `is_alive()` and then calls `terminate()` on each process but never `join()`s them afterward. The diff shows no other cleanup/reaping path for dead processes, so across restart cycles this can accumulate unreaped processes/resources.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Dead code _create_process_for_shard (singular) never kills/reaps the old process and would corrupt state if ever called; it should be removed or routed through the restart path

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `SpanFlusher` adds `_create_process_for_shard(self, shard: int)`, but there are no call sites shown for it (all restarts go through `_ensure_processes_alive()` which directly kills (for `multiprocessing.Process`) and then calls `_create_process_for_shards`). If `_create_process_for_shard` were ever used, it would call `_create_process_for_shards` without first stopping/killing the existing process/thread for that `process_index`, then overwrite `self.processes[process_index]`/`self.buffers[process_index]`, leaving the old worker running and making state inconsistent. As-is it’s dead/unused and not a currently verifiable runtime defect, but it’s a concrete, diff-grounded maintainability/latent-correctness issue.

adjudication_records.issue_text: process_restarts is never reset after sustained health, so one shard's process hitting MAX_PROCESS_RESTARTS cumulatively can crash the whole consumer long after a transient incident

adjudication.rationale: In `SpanFlusher`, `self.process_restarts` is a per-process counter initialized in `__init__` and only ever incremented in `_ensure_processes_alive()` when a process is unhealthy; it is never reset on sustained health (even though `process_healthy_since[...]` is updated). If a single process repeatedly crashes/hangs over a long period (even with long healthy gaps), the cumulative count can eventually exceed `MAX_PROCESS_RESTARTS` and raise `RuntimeError`, restarting the whole consumer. This is a concrete behavior visible in the diff, but it’s more of a resilience/operational policy concern than a clear correctness defect since the “crashed repeatedly” threshold is not specified as needing to decay/reset over time (and the prior single-counter version also did not reset).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Inconsistent metric tag names: produce timer uses tags={"shards": ...} while other metrics use "shard", splitting/losing telemetry on produce latency

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows inconsistent metric tag keys for related flusher latency metrics: `metrics.timer("spans.buffer.flusher.produce", tags={"shard": shard_tag})` uses `shard`, while `metrics.timer("spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce", tags={"shards": shard_tag})` uses `shards`. This will split telemetry/aggregation across two tag names for similar per-shard measurements, reducing usefulness of dashboards/alerts, but it does not directly break runtime behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: New multi-process health/restart logic (restart counter, RuntimeError after MAX_PROCESS_RESTARTS, per-process hang detection in flusher.py _ensure_processes_alive) has zero test coverage despite being the most behaviorally risky change

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds new per-process health/hang detection and restart behavior in `SpanFlusher._ensure_processes_alive` (looping over `self.processes`, checking `process.is_alive()`, hang detection via `process_healthy_since[...]`, incrementing `process_restarts[...]`, and raising `RuntimeError` after `MAX_PROCESS_RESTARTS`). The added tests only cover process limiting/shard distribution (`test_flusher_processes_limit`) and backpressure value existence (`test_flusher`), but do not exercise any unhealthy/hang path, restart counter behavior, or the `RuntimeError` threshold. So the finding about lack of coverage for this risky new logic is supported by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Tests only exercise the threading path because they pass produce_to_pipe=messages.append, so the multiprocessing spawn path (pickling shard_buffer, mp_context.Value handles, process.kill()/terminate()) is never verified

adjudication.rationale: In `SpanFlusher._create_process_for_shards`, the multiprocessing path is only taken when `produce_to_pipe is None` (it uses `self.mp_context.Process` and passes `mp_context.Value`s). All tests in the diff construct the flusher via `ProcessSpansStrategyFactory(..., produce_to_pipe=messages.append)` (e.g. `test_basic` and `test_flusher_processes_limit`), which forces the `threading.Thread` path. Therefore the spawn/pickling logic and `multiprocessing.Process` lifecycle handling (`kill()/terminate()`, `exitcode`, etc.) are not exercised by these tests.

adjudication_records.issue_text: test_flusher_processes_limit verifies structure not behavior — it asserts process count and shard counts but never submits a message or verifies spans from multiplexed shards actually get flushed, and round-robin shard distribution is unasserted

adjudication.rationale: In `test_flusher_processes_limit`, the assertions only cover internal structure (`len(flusher.processes)`, `max_processes`, `num_processes`, and total assigned shards) and never exercise the new multi-process/shard-routing behavior by submitting messages and validating that spans from shards handled by a shared process are actually flushed/produced. It also doesn’t assert the intended round-robin mapping (it only checks `total_shards == 4`, not how they are distributed across the two processes). This is a concrete gap given the new logic in `SpanFlusher.__init__` that builds `process_to_shards_map` and spawns per-shard-group workers.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Weakened assertion in test_flusher backpressure test: changed from checking aggregate backpressure_since.value to any(x.value for per-process values), so aggregate backpressure behavior in submit() raising MessageRejected is not verified and there is no test for MessageRejected on single-process sustained backpressure

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes the implementation from a single `backpressure_since` value to per-process values (`process_backpressure_since`), and `submit()` now raises `MessageRejected` if *any* process has sustained backpressure. Updating the test assertion from `flusher.backpressure_since.value` to `any(x.value for x in flusher.process_backpressure_since.values())` aligns with the new design rather than “weakening” it. The finding’s claims about aggregate backpressure behavior and lack of `MessageRejected` verification are not demonstrated by the shown diff (and the prior assertion also didn’t verify `MessageRejected`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Missing edge-case test: empty assigned_shards causes ZeroDivisionError at construction because num_processes = min(max_processes, len(assigned_shards)) can be 0 and i % num_processes divides by zero

adjudication.rationale: In `SpanFlusher.__init__`, `self.num_processes = min(self.max_processes, len(buffer.assigned_shards))` can be 0 when `assigned_shards` is empty, but the only modulo operation (`process_index = i % self.num_processes`) occurs inside `for i, shard in enumerate(buffer.assigned_shards):`. If `assigned_shards` is empty, that loop never runs, so no `ZeroDivisionError` is triggered by this diff as claimed.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Flaky timing in test_basic: fixed time.sleep(0.1) with no synchronization guaranteeing the flusher thread completed, making (msg,) = messages assertion racy on slow CI — should use explicit wait/poll loop

adjudication.rationale: In `test_basic`, the added `time.sleep(0.1)` is intended to “give flusher threads time to process”, but earlier in the same test `monkeypatch.setattr("time.sleep", lambda _: None)` makes that sleep a no-op. That means there is no real synchronization between advancing `current_drift`/calling `step.poll()` and later asserting `(msg,) = messages`, so the test can become racy depending on whether the background flusher thread(s) have appended to `messages` yet.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No test for flusher_processes CLI wiring: the --flusher-processes click option → factory parameter → SpanFlusher(max_processes=...) chain is untested, so name/param drift would go unnoticed

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new click option in `ingest_transactions_options()` (`click.Option(["--flusher-processes", "flusher_processes"], ...)`) and threads it via `ProcessSpansStrategyFactory(flusher_processes=...)` to `SpanFlusher(max_processes=...)`. The new tests only cover passing `flusher_processes` directly into `ProcessSpansStrategyFactory` (`test_flusher_processes_limit`), not the CLI/click option wiring path, so a drift/mismatch in the click option name/param mapping could go untested.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Dead code: `_create_process_for_shard` in flusher.py is never called and duplicates process-lookup logic, risking divergence

adjudication.rationale: In `src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py`, the method `_create_process_for_shard(self, shard: int)` is newly added but there is no call site shown in the diff (the restart path in `_ensure_processes_alive` calls `_create_process_for_shards(process_index, shards)` directly). The helper also repeats the process-index lookup by iterating `self.process_to_shards_map`, which duplicates logic already available where `process_index` is known, creating an avoidable maintenance/divergence risk. This is a real diff-grounded cleanup concern, not a functional defect by itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Inconsistent metric tag key: `wait_produce` uses `tags={"shards": shard_tag}` while other metrics use `"shard"`, fragmenting metrics and breaking dashboards/alerts
Test's added `time.sleep(0.1)` is a no-op because `time.sleep` is globally monkeypatched, providing no synchronization and risking flaky tests
matched_golden_ids: The test_basic function in test_consumer.py uses a monkeypatched time.sleep that returns immediately, but then calls time.sleep(0.1) expecting it to actually wait.
Sleep in test_consumer.py won’t actually wait because time.sleep was monkeypatched above; consider restoring sleep or using a different sync to ensure the flusher has time to process.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both point out that `time.sleep` has been monkeypatched to return immediately, so calling `time.sleep(0.1)` in `test_basic` does not actually wait/synchronize as intended, which can lead to flaky behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Unrelated drive-by change to CLAUDE.md (hasattr vs isinstance guidance) bundled into this PR, muddying review and git blame

adjudication.rationale: The diff includes a standalone documentation change in `CLAUDE.md` adding guidance about `hasattr()` vs `isinstance()` for unions, while the rest of the PR changes span flusher multiprocessing behavior and related tests/options. This CLAUDE.md edit is unrelated to the functional changes and would reasonably be considered a scope/review/blame muddying drive-by change bundled into the PR.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No validation of `flusher_processes` / `max_processes`: negative `max_processes` yields zero flusher processes with no error, `0` is silently coerced via `or` fallback inconsistently with CLI semantics

adjudication.rationale: In `SpanFlusher.__init__`, `self.max_processes = max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)` means `0` is silently treated as “unset” and replaced with `len(assigned_shards)`, which is inconsistent with an explicit CLI-provided value. Also, negative values are not validated: `self.num_processes = min(self.max_processes, len(...))` can become negative, leading to an empty `process_to_shards_map` (`range(self.num_processes)`) and then a runtime failure when assigning shards (`self.process_to_shards_map[process_index].append(shard)`). This is an actual correctness issue introduced by the diff (even if the finding’s specific claim about ‘zero processes with no error’ is imprecise).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Restart path leaks hung threads / duplicate flushers for same shards: threads cannot be killed, and the `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)` guard makes the kill a silent no-op for threads

adjudication.rationale: In `SpanFlusher._create_process_for_shards`, when `produce_to_pipe` is provided it uses `threading.Thread` (not a `multiprocessing.Process`) as the worker (`make_process = threading.Thread`). In `_ensure_processes_alive`, on detected hang (`time.time() - process_healthy_since[...] > max_unhealthy_seconds`) it attempts to stop the worker via `if isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process): process.kill()`, which is a no-op for threads, and then unconditionally calls `_create_process_for_shards(...)` to start a replacement. This can leave the original hung thread running and create a second flusher for the same shard set (duplicate flushers / thread leak). The diff provides no other mechanism to stop or join hung threads before restart.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Misleading dead comment `# Check if any shard handled by this process is unhealthy` precedes a plain `cause = "hang"` with no per-shard check and should be deleted

adjudication.rationale: The diff does contain the comment `# Check if any shard handled by this process is unhealthy` immediately before setting `cause = "hang"` based solely on `process_healthy_since[...]` (no per-shard health check). However, this is a documentation/comment accuracy nit rather than a verifiable correctness defect or substantial review issue created by the change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Duplicated metric-emission loops across `submit` paths couple submit's backpressure logic to internal shard→process partitioning; should be extracted into aggregate helpers

adjudication.rationale: The diff does add loops in `SpanFlusher.submit()` over `self.buffers.values()` and `self.process_backpressure_since.values()` to aggregate state across processes, but there are not “duplicated metric-emission loops across submit paths” shown. Metrics emission per-shard occurs in `_ensure_processes_alive()` (a separate method), and `submit()` only emits a single `spans.buffer.flusher.backpressure` increment when any process exceeds the threshold. The finding’s premise about duplicated metric-emission loops is not grounded in the diff and the “extract into helpers” suggestion is too vague/architectural to verify as a concrete issue.

adjudication_records.issue_text: join() timeout path breaks out of the loop, skipping terminate() for current and remaining flusher processes, causing partial-failure shutdown regression (process 1 terminated, processes 2..N not)

adjudication.rationale: In `SpanFlusher.join()`, when a timeout/deadline is provided, the loop over processes does `if remaining_time <= 0: break`, which exits the *entire* `for process_index, process in self.processes.items()` loop. Since the `process.terminate()` call is inside that loop, any not-yet-iterated flusher processes will not be terminated, leaving them running on partial-timeout shutdown (only earlier processes may be terminated). This matches the reported partial-failure shutdown regression.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Group restart cascade in _ensure_processes_alive: a hung shard kills and restarts its whole process group, dragging healthy sibling shards down on every restart cycle

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly groups multiple shards into a single flusher worker via `process_to_shards_map` and creates one process/thread per group (`_create_process_for_shards`). Health is tracked only per process (`process_healthy_since[process_index]`), and on `hang` or dead process, `_ensure_processes_alive` restarts that entire process with all its assigned `shards` (`_create_process_for_shards(process_index, shards)`). So if a single shard’s work causes the process to stop making progress, the restart necessarily affects all sibling shards in that same process group. This is a real design/operational concern introduced by the new shard-to-process multiplexing, but it’s not a strictly verifiable correctness defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Per-group restart counter means a flapping group trips MAX_PROCESS_RESTARTS and raises RuntimeError, restarting the consumer and punishing shards that were fine

adjudication.rationale: In `SpanFlusher._ensure_processes_alive`, restart tracking is per `process_index` via `self.process_restarts[process_index]`, but once any single process exceeds `MAX_PROCESS_RESTARTS` it raises `RuntimeError(...)` ("restarting consumer"). That exception would restart/stop the whole consumer even though other process groups (and their shards) may still be healthy, so one flapping shard-group can take down all shards handled by this consumer instance. This is a real behavior implied by the diff, but it’s a design/operational concern rather than a strictly verifiable correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Shared healthy_since is only updated after a full loop over all shards, so a shard that repeatedly hangs-and-recovers under a fast sibling never accumulates unhealthy time — shard-level hang detection effectively never fires

adjudication.rationale: The diff does not implement shard-level hang detection via separate `healthy_since` values per shard. Instead, it introduces `process_healthy_since[process_index]` and checks health per-process in `_ensure_processes_alive()`. In `SpanFlusher.main()`, `healthy_since.value` is updated every loop iteration (before the `if not flushed_segments` sleep/continue), not only “after a full loop over all shards.” While one could argue per-shard health isn’t tracked when multiple shards share a process, the finding’s specific claim about a shared `healthy_since` updated only after looping all shards is not supported by the shown code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Hung thread-mode flushers are never actually killed: the kill is guarded by isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process) so it's a no-op for threading.Thread, while a new thread is still spawned for the same shards, allowing N hung threads to accumulate and poll the same shard groups concurrently, with double-produce risk if a hung thread wakes after the replacement flushed segments

adjudication.rationale: In `SpanFlusher._ensure_processes_alive`, when a flusher is unhealthy it attempts to stop it via `if isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process): process.kill()` and then immediately calls `_create_process_for_shards(...)` to spawn a replacement. In thread-mode (`produce_to_pipe is not None`), `_create_process_for_shards` uses `threading.Thread`, so the kill path is a no-op and the old hung thread is not stopped (no other stop signal is set during restart besides the shared `stopped` flag, which is only set in `join`). This means repeated unhealthy detections can create multiple threads for the same shard group (`process_to_shards_map`), accumulating and potentially running concurrently.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Metrics tag typo: wait_produce metric uses tags={"shards": shard_tag} while every other metric uses "shard", splitting the metric into a separate tag family and breaking dashboards/alerts
matched_golden_ids: In the SpanFlusher flush loop, metric tags inconsistently use 'shard' (e.g., in spans.buffer.flusher.produce and spans.buffer.segment_size_bytes) and 'shards' (in spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce) for the same shard identifier value. This prevents correct metric aggregation across flush stages — dashboards and alerts filtering by tag 'shard' will miss data tagged as 'shards' and vice versa.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate issue flags the same inconsistency in metric tag keys: wait_produce uses "shards" while other metrics use "shard", which splits aggregation and breaks dashboards/alerts. This matches the golden comment’s underlying problem exactly.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Dead/incorrect method _create_process_for_shard is never called and its semantics (restart entire group for one shard) invite misuse by future callers; should be deleted or made to delegate to the group path

adjudication.rationale: In `src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py` the new helper `def _create_process_for_shard(self, shard: int):` is defined but no call sites are shown anywhere in the diff (only `_create_processes`, `_create_process_for_shards`, and `_ensure_processes_alive` are used). That makes it dead code as introduced. Also, its behavior is to restart the entire process handling the shard’s group (`_create_process_for_shards(process_index, shards)`), which could be misleading for future callers expecting a shard-scoped restart. This is a maintainability/architecture issue rather than a directly verifiable runtime defect in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Metrics cardinality explosion: segment_size_bytes and flusher_unhealthy now tag raw shard numbers, and flusher_unhealthy fires per shard per unhealthy event, multiplying series cardinality with many partitions

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds per-shard (and per-shard-group) metric tags and multiplies emission: `segment_size_bytes` and `spans.buffer.flusher.produce` now include `tags={"shard": shard_tag}` where `shard_tag` is a raw comma-joined list of shard IDs (`main(): shard_tag = ",".join(...)`). Additionally, `_ensure_processes_alive` increments `spans.buffer.flusher_unhealthy` once per shard with `tags={"cause": cause, "shard": shard}`. With many partitions/shards this can increase metric series cardinality and event volume. This is a concrete, diff-grounded observability/cost concern rather than a functional defect.
